title: Vision Transformers and Multimodal Meaning · Level 2
slo: Explain how image and text information can be connected in a multimodal model.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence obscures which embeddings are connected.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the technique, then state the relationship, the two embedding types, and the shared space.

exercises.correct_answer: Cross-model attention relates language embeddings with vision embeddings in shared space
exercises.explanation: Cross-model attention relates language embeddings with vision embeddings in shared space.

exercises.question_text: The embedding set that represents relationships among words is a ___.

parts.text: The embedding set that represents relationships among words is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That term refers to images or multimodal space rather than word relationships.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use language vocabulary for embeddings that relate words.

exercises.explanation: Language-transformer embeddings form a language vocabulary.

exercises.question_text: A smart-checkout team wants camera features and produce-description words to connect in one representation. Which choices should the team make? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Cross-model attention relates language embeddings to vision embeddings. It is needed to define their cross-modal relationships.
A shared vector space supplies one unified representation. It lets language and visual embeddings be related spatially.
A single image class predicts a category for an image. It does not connect camera features with description words.
options.better_fit: A single image class is appropriate for basic image classification.

feedback.intrinsic: The checkout could name an item without connecting it to language.
feedback.instructional: Use cross-model attention and shared vector space for multimodal links.

options.rationale: Pixel labels identify classes for image areas. They do not establish relationships between visual and language embeddings.
options.better_fit: Pixel object labels are appropriate for semantic segmentation.

feedback.intrinsic: The checkout could outline an object while lacking a language connection.
feedback.instructional: Shared-space modeling links vision embeddings with language embeddings.

exercises.explanation: These choices connect language and vision in one representation.

exercises.question_text: A retailer wants to organize the meanings of product-description words such as “apple” and “banana.” Which vocabulary should its AI team use?

options.rationale: Language vocabulary represents semantic relationships among written words. It can organize related product-description terms.
Visual vocabulary represents relationships among image features. It would organize appearance patterns rather than word meanings.
options.better_fit: Visual vocabulary is appropriate for relating features in photos of produce.

feedback.intrinsic: This would organize visual appearance instead of word meanings.
feedback.instructional: Choose language vocabulary when relating written words.

options.rationale: A feature map is an image-side representation of extracted patterns. It is not a vocabulary of semantic word relationships.
options.better_fit: A feature map is appropriate when processing extracted visual information from an image.

feedback.intrinsic: This would shift the task from language to image filtering.
feedback.instructional: Language vocabulary comes from embeddings of words.

options.rationale: A bounding box marks an object's image location. It does not organize the meanings of product names.
options.better_fit: A bounding box is appropriate when locating a product in a photo.

feedback.intrinsic: This could locate an item but not organize its name.
feedback.instructional: Language vocabulary represents relationships among words.

exercises.explanation: Product-description words belong in a language vocabulary.

exercises.question_text: Training data that links a photo to its written description is called ___.

parts.text: Training data that links a photo to its written description is called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice lacks the image-description pairing.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Class labels and bounding boxes serve classification and detection, not image-text pairing.

exercises.correct_answer: ["paired image-text data","paired images and text","images paired with text descriptions"]
exercises.explanation: Paired image-text data associates every image with a written description.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the steps to describe an unfamiliar image.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The description would be attempted before language was connected to image features.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The process proceeds from visual recognition through shared-space retrieval to description.

exercises.correct_answer: Recognize visual features search shared space find associated language produce a description
exercises.explanation: Recognize features first, use shared space to find language, then produce the description.

exercises.question_text: A grocery retailer has produce photos and matching written descriptions and wants to connect what it sees with words. What can this data help build?

options.rationale: Paired photos and descriptions can combine language and vision encoders. Their combination forms a multimodal model.
An image-only classifier predicts categories from image inputs. It does not connect images with written descriptions.
options.better_fit: An image-only classifier is appropriate for identifying a fruit type from a photo.

feedback.intrinsic: The retailer would get a label without a language connection.
feedback.instructional: Paired image-text data supports a multimodal model.

options.rationale: Segmentation assigns labels to image pixels. Matching written descriptions do not provide the needed pixel-level targets.
options.better_fit: A pixel segmentation model is appropriate for finding precise object regions.

feedback.intrinsic: The retailer could obtain object areas without connecting words and images.

options.rationale: A bounding-box detector predicts object locations. It does not model image-description relationships.
options.better_fit: A bounding-box detector is appropriate for locating multiple products in an image.

feedback.intrinsic: The retailer could find regions but not connect them to language.

exercises.explanation: The paired data can build a multimodal model.

exercises.question_text: A doorbell-camera service receives a new photo and must provide a useful written description. Which actions should its combined model use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The model needs visual features from the new photo. They provide the basis for linking image content to language.

options.text: Find related language in shared space
options.rationale: Shared space relates visual features to language representations. Finding related language enables a written description.
The linked visual and language information supports description generation. This meets the service's need for useful written output.
One class label yields only a narrow category name. It cannot provide the requested useful written description.
options.better_fit: Returning one class label is appropriate for simple image classification.

feedback.intrinsic: The resident would receive only a category name.
feedback.instructional: A useful description links visual features with associated language.

exercises.explanation: The model should recognize features, connect them to language, and generate a description.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence no longer states the relationship clearly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the features, then state their co-occurrence, relationship, and limitation.

exercises.correct_answer: Visual features that occur together can be contextually related without human understanding
exercises.explanation: Co-occurring visual features can be contextually related without human-like understanding.

exercises.question_text: Vectors that represent image features and their contextual relationships are called ___.

parts.text: Vectors that represent image features and their contextual relationships are called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That term does not name the vectors themselves.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use visual embeddings for the vector representations; visual vocabulary is the map formed from them.

exercises.explanation: Visual embeddings are vectors representing visual features and their contextual relationships.

exercises.question_text: A doorbell-camera developer finds hat-like features repeatedly near head-like features. Which conclusions should the developer make? Select all that apply.

options.text: The features may be contextually related
options.rationale: Repeated proximity can indicate a learned contextual relationship. The conclusion concerns the visual patterns, not object comprehension.

options.text: The model can relate their visual patterns
options.rationale: The model can represent associations among recurring visual characteristics. This is a valid interpretation of the observed co-occurrence.

options.text: The model has human understanding of hats
options.rationale: Pattern association does not establish human-style conceptual understanding. The model has learned a visual relationship rather than a human concept of hats.
options.better_fit: This claim is appropriate when describing a person who understands what a hat is.

feedback.intrinsic: This would make an unsupported claim about the camera.
feedback.instructional: Treat the result as a relationship among visual patterns.

options.text: The model has assigned one class label
options.rationale: A contextual relationship is not a category prediction. The evidence describes co-occurring features rather than one assigned label.
options.better_fit: A class label is appropriate when an image-classification system predicts a category.

feedback.intrinsic: This reduces a feature relationship to a category name.
feedback.instructional: Contextual relatedness connects recurring visual features.

exercises.explanation: The patterns may be contextually related without implying human understanding.

exercises.question_text: A grocery-store engineer needs a camera representation that relates color, shape, and texture across produce-image patches. What should the engineer use?

options.rationale: Visual embeddings represent color, shape, and texture in image patches. They retain relationships among those visual features.
A language vocabulary represents relationships among words. It would not directly represent produce-image features.
options.better_fit: A language vocabulary is appropriate for organizing product-description words.

feedback.intrinsic: The system would focus on words instead of the produce image.
feedback.instructional: Use visual embeddings to represent image-patch features.

options.rationale: One image label supplies a category prediction. It does not provide a detailed representation of feature relationships.
options.better_fit: One image label is appropriate for a basic classification task.

feedback.intrinsic: The result would be a category rather than a rich representation.
feedback.instructional: Visual embeddings retain relationships among visual features.

options.rationale: A class target is a known answer used during supervised training. It is not the representation computed from image patches.
options.better_fit: A class target is appropriate when training a classifier with labeled examples.

feedback.intrinsic: The engineer would use a training answer instead of image information.
feedback.instructional: Visual embeddings are the representations used for visual features.

exercises.explanation: Visual embeddings relate visual features across patches.
